original_question: For the planar symplectic billiard in a stadium-shaped domain, is the dynamics chaotic?
target_in_paper: Serge Tabachnikov, Problem 3, Question 3: "Is the symplectic billiard dynamic in the stadium chaotic?" The immediately preceding setup defines the planar symplectic billiard as a dynamical system on oriented chords, with the reflection law shown in Fig. 7. ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/022-0198.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct object (the planar symplectic billiard), the correct special table singled out in the paper (the stadium), and the correct qualitative issue (chaotic behavior). So it is very close to the paper’s actual open problem. ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/022-0198.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s setup is a map on oriented boundary chords, not just an unspecified billiard dynamics in a domain; that phase space should be stated explicitly. ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/022-0198.pdf))

The defining reflection rule should be included: if the oriented chord x y reflects to y z, then the tangent line to the boundary at y is parallel to x z (Fig. 7). ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/022-0198.pdf))

The paper says only "the stadium" and does not define it, so a stand-alone version should specify the standard planar stadium (Bunimovich stadium), i.e. the convex domain bounded by two parallel line segments joined by semicircular arcs.

"Chaotic" is left informal in the paper; no rigorous substitute such as ergodicity, positive entropy, uniform hyperbolicity, or mixing is specified there. A refined stand-alone question should preserve this ambiguity only if one wants to remain maximally faithful to the paper. ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/022-0198.pdf))

It is implicit that the map is considered on the set of chords for which the tangent used in the reflection law is defined and the next chord is well defined; the paper does not spell out a singular set or exclusions. ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/022-0198.pdf))

No extra hypotheses such as genericity, perturbative regime, smooth approximation, or parameter range are imposed in the paper; the question is specifically about the stadium case itself. ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/022-0198.pdf))
No algebraic data such as ambient field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifiers appear in this problem; the omitted details are geometric and dynamical rather than algebraic.
refined_question: For the planar symplectic billiard map on oriented chords of the standard stadium (the convex planar domain bounded by two parallel line segments joined by semicircular arcs), where an oriented chord x y is followed by y z whenever the tangent line to the boundary at y is parallel to x z, does this map exhibit chaotic dynamics? ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/022-0198.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting exactly Serge Tabachnikov’s Problem 3, Question 3, rather than a broader neighboring problem. The surrounding text first defines planar symplectic billiards as dynamics on oriented chords and gives the reflection law in Fig. 7; only then does it ask about the stadium and add the brief contextual remark that numerics suggest chaos. Since the paper itself does not formalize "chaotic" and does not state any equivalent reformulation, the faithful sharpening is to make explicit the phase space, the stadium table, and the reflection law, while keeping the scope no broader than the original open question. ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/022-0198.pdf))
